reports.title: Performance Audit on Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) – Skill India

paras.heading: Unspent Funds Under PMKVY State Components
paras.finding_summary: As of July 2023, ₹337.16 crore remained unutilised across states under PMKVY 2.0 and 3.0. About 20% of funds released for state components remained unspent as of March 2024.
paras.report_no: Report No. 20 of 2025 – PMKVY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Invalid Beneficiary Bank Account Data
paras.finding_summary: Bank account details were missing, blank, null, or marked 'N/A' for 90.66 lakh out of 95.90 lakh beneficiaries — over 94% of records. Email IDs and bank accounts of ~95% of candidates were invalid or missing in the Skill India Portal (SIP).
paras.report_no: Report No. 20 of 2025 – PMKVY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Low Placement Rates and Fake Certifications
paras.finding_summary: Of 56.14 lakh candidates certified under Short Term Training and Special Projects, only 23.18 lakh (41%) found placements. For technical roles, 85.40% of certified candidates had only basic literacy. Certifications awarded through non-existent or ineligible agencies.
paras.report_no: Report No. 20 of 2025 – PMKVY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Irregular Administrative Expense Charges and Interest Recovery
paras.finding_summary: ₹24.13 crore was overcharged as administrative expenses under PMKVY 1.0. Implementing agency retained interest of ₹12.16 crore on released funds, which was subsequently recovered. Delayed transfer of ₹222.63 crore identified.
paras.report_no: Report No. 20 of 2025 – PMKVY Performance Audit

paras.heading: State-wise Unspent Funds – Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha
paras.finding_summary: Bihar: of ₹36.82 crore released, only ₹5.96 crore was utilised by March 2024 due to lack of training centres and absence of skill-gap studies. Maharashtra: ₹18.94 crore unspent from ₹136.51 crore. Odisha: ₹20.33 crore refunded with ₹6.39 crore interest.
paras.report_no: Report No. 20 of 2025 – PMKVY Performance Audit

reports.title: Performance Audit on Jal Jeevan Mission (Kerala, 2019–2024)

paras.heading: Financial Management Lapses and Fund Utilisation
paras.finding_summary: Lapses in financial management of the scheme, with issues around fund sources and utilisation. National BE for JJM was ₹67,000 crore but RE was slashed to ₹17,000 crore in 2025-26 — a 75% cut — reflecting systemic underspending.
paras.report_no: Report No. 10 of 2025 – JJM Performance Audit

paras.heading: Procurement Lapses and Limited Competition
paras.finding_summary: Several instances where tendering norms were not followed or contracts awarded with limited competition. Procurement lapses account for a large share of complaints under JJM.
paras.report_no: Report No. 10 of 2025 – JJM Performance Audit

paras.heading: Inadequate Water Pressure and Asset Quality
paras.finding_summary: Water pressure in several schemes was inadequate, leading to quick deterioration of newly created assets. Quality of drinking water varied across districts despite massive spend.
paras.report_no: Report No. 10 of 2025 – JJM Performance Audit

paras.heading: Overstatement of Housing Completion — 77 of 2,079 Houses Actually Complete
paras.finding_summary: Physical verification of 2,079 houses shown as 'completed' in PMAY-G MIS found only 77 houses actually complete on ground. Despite state reporting 34.18 lakh houses as completed, 20,215 remained incomplete as of March 2025. Serious disconnect between reported and actual completion.
paras.report_no: Report No. 8 of 2025 – PMAY-G UP Performance Audit

paras.heading: Poor Quality Houses — Missing Toilets, Electricity, Water
paras.finding_summary: Tens of thousands of houses claimed as 'complete' found to be of poor quality or missing essential amenities including toilets, electricity connections, and water supply, in violation of scheme norms.
paras.report_no: Report No. 8 of 2025 – PMAY-G UP Performance Audit

paras.heading: ₹230 Crore Blocked Due to Geo-Tagging and Social Audit Issues
paras.finding_summary: Over ₹230 crore remained blocked due to geo-tagging failures and social audit issues. Significant funds stuck and beneficiaries remained unpaid due to delays in fund transfers, inadequate verification, and unresolved payout issues.
paras.report_no: Report No. 8 of 2025 – PMAY-U Chhattisgarh Performance Audit

paras.heading: Ineligible Beneficiaries and Duplicate Housing Benefits
paras.finding_summary: 71 beneficiaries with annual incomes exceeding ₹3 lakh (above PMAY-U ceiling) were allotted houses. ₹4.05 crore released to 250 beneficiaries without verifying land ownership. 99 beneficiaries received both PMAY-G and PMAY-U benefits; 35 received benefits under an earlier programme too.
paras.report_no: Report No. 8 of 2025 – PMAY-U Chhattisgarh Performance Audit

reports.title: Performance Audit on Ayushman Bharat – PM Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)

paras.heading: Excess Payments to Hospitals
paras.finding_summary: In Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, and Tamil Nadu, excess payment of ₹57.53 crore made to hospitals for claims under PMJAY. Ineligible households registered as beneficiaries availed benefits ranging between ₹0.12 lakh to ₹22.44 crore.
paras.report_no: Report No. 11 of 2023 – AB-PMJAY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Claims Paid for Deceased Patients
paras.finding_summary: 88,760 patients were shown as having died during treatment but 2,14,923 claims were paid for fresh treatment of these same patients. Maximum cases in Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Jharkhand, Kerala, and Madhya Pradesh.
paras.report_no: Report No. 11 of 2023 – AB-PMJAY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Diversion of Scheme Funds by State Health Agencies
paras.finding_summary: 7 State Health Agencies (SHAs) diverted grants of ₹50.61 crore from one head to another. 6 SHAs furnished inflated Utilization Certificates amounting to ₹38.24 crore to the National Health Authority. ₹96.63 crore still lying in the RSBY fund.
paras.report_no: Report No. 11 of 2023 – AB-PMJAY Performance Audit

paras.heading: Beneficiaries Charged Out-of-Pocket Despite Cashless Mandate
paras.finding_summary: In Meghalaya, 13,418 of 19,459 beneficiaries (69%) had to pay an additional ₹12.34 crore at discharge despite PMJAY being a cashless scheme. Scheme is supposed to provide health cover up to ₹5 lakh per family.
paras.report_no: Report No. 11 of 2023 – AB-PMJAY Performance Audit

reports.title: CAG Report on Public Health Sector – Unspent Funds Over Five Years

paras.heading: ₹9,122 Crore Unspent in Health Ministry in 2023-24
paras.finding_summary: Department of Health and Family Welfare spent ₹95,561 crore against approved provision of ₹1,04,683 crore — leaving ₹9,122.15 crore unutilised in 2023-24. In 2022-23, ₹14,472.40 crore was unspent. Recurring pattern of underspending despite modest allocations. Health Research dept left ₹121.85 crore unspent in 2023-24.
paras.report_no: Report No. 4 of 2025 – Public Health Sector

reports.title: Compliance Audit – Centrally Sponsored Schemes SNA Fund Management

paras.heading: ₹346 Crore Lying Unspent in SNA Bank Accounts
paras.finding_summary: ₹346.35 crore lying unspent in bank accounts of State Nodal Agencies (SNAs) as on 31 March — adversely impacting quality of accounts. Central share ₹916.92 crore and State share ₹117.56 crore transferred via Fully Vouched Contingent Bills without actual expenditure vouchers received by AG office.
paras.report_no: CAG Report No. 7 of 2025 – Compliance Audit Civil

paras.heading: ₹6,222 Crore Parked Outside Consolidated Fund in SNA Accounts (PFMS Data)
paras.finding_summary: As per PFMS portal data, ₹6,222.10 crore (₹3,069.44 crore being Government of India share) was parked in SNA bank accounts outside the Consolidated Fund of India. Reduces accountability and earns interest outside Treasury.
paras.report_no: CAG Report No. 7 of 2025 – Compliance Audit Civil

paras.heading: Total Unspent Budget Across All Ministries 2021-22
paras.scheme: All Centrally Sponsored and Central Sector Schemes
paras.finding_summary: Against total budget provision of ₹6,12,570.29 crore in 2021-22, Ministries/Departments had overall unspent budget of ₹39,167.11 crore — 6.39% of total grant/appropriation.
paras.report_no: CAG Report – Union Government Finance Accounts 2021-22

reports.title: Compliance Audit Report – Finance & Communication (BSNL, SAMEER)
reports.ministry: Ministry of Communications / Ministry of Electronics & IT

paras.heading: BSNL Revenue Loss on Jio Infrastructure Sharing
paras.finding_summary: BSNL failed to enforce Master Service Agreement with Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd and did not bill for additional technology on shared infrastructure. Loss of ₹1,757.76 crore and penal interest from May 2014 to March 2024.
paras.report_no: Report No. 1 of 2025 – Finance & Communication

reports.title: CAG Audit on GST – Systemic Inconsistencies in Tax Collections

paras.heading: ₹21,695 Crore GST Inconsistencies — ITC Mismatches
paras.finding_summary: CAG audit exposed inconsistencies worth ₹21,695 crore in GST collections. Systemic failures including mismatches in input tax credit, compliance deviations in over 2,519 cases, and short payments of tax and interest.
paras.report_no: CAG Report on GST – December 2025
